rules.rationale: Electronegative halide p states lie deep below the Fermi level, widening ionic gaps.
Main-group oxides lack partially filled d bands, keeping conduction edges high and gaps wide.
Polarizable S, Se, Te p states raise the valence-band edge, systematically narrowing gaps.
Low mean atomic number means compact orbitals and weak spin-orbit splitting, favoring wide gaps.

skills.hypothesis: Target-native ionic wide-gap chemistry: electronegative closed-shell anions with light main-group cations, penalizing polarizable chalcogenides. Fails if the halide subset is too small or if d0 transition-metal oxides dominate the extreme top.

rules.rationale: Largest source refractive-index effect; Moss relation ties high polarizability to narrow experimental gaps.
Halogen dominance depressed source refractive index, which by Moss inversion predicts wide ionic gaps.
Heavy elements gave the top mean_z source effect; larger polarizability and spin-orbit splitting shrink gaps.
Balanced compositions gave the largest source positive effect and favor wide-gap ordered insulators.

skills.hypothesis: Counter-hypothesis inverting source refractive-index signs through the Moss relation, dropping near-zero-confidence lanthanide and transition-metal transfers. Fails if experimental gaps here track structure or reporting artifacts rather than composition-driven polarizability.

state.lesson: Source evidence is refractive index, physically anti-correlated with band gap via the Moss relation, and its per-field confidences are weak. Same-sign transfer would chase narrow-gap polarizable chemistries, so the target-native ionic wide-gap prior carries higher confidence and larger early semantic mass, while the inverted-transfer skill remains the lower-confidence counter-hypothesis.
state.revision_summary: Reconsidered both proposals using only the original source-transfer evidence and schema, since no measured development feedback exists. Kept the domain-knowledge ionic wide-gap skill with the same rule set and only minor weight and mass adjustments. Rebuilt the counter-hypothesis as a Moss-inversion skill: metalloid, halogen, and mean_z_high rules retained from the strongest source effects, the weakly supported pnictide sign-reversal rule replaced by the higher-support balanced-stoichiometry positive, and near-zero-confidence lanthanide and transition-metal transfers dropped. All conditions map real catalog fields to exact catalog values; weights, ridge, prior scale, semantic masses, betas, xi, and confidences stay inside allowed ranges. No target outcomes or candidate identifiers are used.
